article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Watermelon Zkittlez × Lemon Tree #11
Breeder: Midwest Best
THC Content: 20–28%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Beta-caryophyllene , D-limonene
Primary Flavors: Lemon, watermelon, sweet citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: Medium to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Melonade tastes almost exactly like its name suggests, yet the genetics behind that flavor are more interesting than a simple fruit-themed marijuana strain . Tart lemon cuts through ripe melon sweetness, creating an aroma closer to freshly squeezed citrus over watermelon candy than the thick dessert character associated with Cookies-heavy weed. That brightness carries into the high. Rather than immediately slowing the body, the cultivar tends to push attention outward, lifting mood and sharpening sensory interest before a gentler physical calm begins to develop. Its reputation was established quickly: Alien Labs’ selected Melonade took first place for Best Sativa Flower at the 2018 Central Valley Cannabis Cup, giving the strain competition credentials before it became widely familiar to cannabis consumers.
Genetics and Lineage

Midwest Best created Melonade by pairing Watermelon Zkittlez with Lemon Tree #11. The breeding process was more specific than the shortened Watermelon Z × Lemon Tree notation seen on dispensary labels. Breeder-history documentation identifies a Watermelon Zkittlez female grown from Dying Breed Seeds stock and a Lemon Tree #11 clone that was reversed to produce pollen. Midwest Best then worked with Alien Labs during the selection process, and Alien Labs retained the expression that became closely associated with the strain’s commercial identity.

Those parents contribute sharply contrasting qualities. Watermelon Zkittlez brings soft fruit, candy sweetness, resin production, and the melon character responsible for half the cultivar’s name. Lemon Tree moves in a much more acidic direction, contributing citrus peel, sharp lemon, subtle gas, and a brighter psychoactive character. The selected offspring manages to preserve both sides without allowing the sugary parent to bury the sour one. In well-grown flower, sweet melon and penetrating lemon remain identifiable at the same time.

Competition success helped validate the selection. At the 2018 Central Valley Cannabis Cup, Melonade by Alien Labs placed first in the Best Sativa Flower category, ahead of Super Lemon Haze and Shoreline. That award became a defining part of the cultivar’s history and helped establish it as valuable breeding material for later hybrids.
Effects and Experience

Melonade usually begins above the shoulders. A quick change in mood can make conversation easier, mundane activities more engaging, and music or visual entertainment considerably more absorbing. Mental energy tends to increase rather than collapse, yet the experience is often smoother than the sharp rush associated with some old-school Haze varieties. The effect fits the modern meaning of a functional sativa: animated and euphoric without necessarily becoming chaotic at a sensible dose.

After the initial lift, a quieter physical component develops underneath. The body may relax while the mind remains alert, producing a useful middle ground for an afternoon, social evening, creative session, gaming, or outdoor leisure. Larger amounts gradually reduce that clarity, making the experience dreamier and less task-oriented. Alien Labs classifies its cut as a sativa and emphasizes the intensely fruity citrus-melon identity of the flower.

THC levels can reach well into the 20% range, so the strain should not be mistaken for light cannabis simply because the flavor is approachable. Excessive intake can cause dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, racing thoughts, or temporary anxiety in THC-sensitive consumers. Lower amounts generally preserve more of the energetic qualities that built Melonade’s reputation.
Medical Benefits

For medical marijuana consumers, the brighter mental effect may be appealing when daytime stress, low mood, or fatigue makes heavily sedating weed undesirable. The strain’s euphoric phase can create a temporary sense of mental distance from everyday tension, while the physical relaxation that develops later may suit people looking to unwind without immediately becoming sleepy.

THC-dominant cannabis is also used by some patients for appetite loss, nausea, discomfort, and mood-related symptoms. Those broader applications should not be confused with clinical evidence for Melonade itself. No controlled trial has established this named cultivar as a treatment for anxiety, depression, chronic pain, ADHD, or another specific condition.

Because potency can vary substantially between harvests, medical users should pay closer attention to the laboratory results on the actual product than to a generic strain average. High-THC cannabis can worsen anxiety or cause impairment in some individuals, and anyone combining marijuana with prescription medication should discuss use with an appropriate healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Few modern cultivars integrate their two parent flavors as clearly as Melonade. The first aroma from the jar can resemble freshly cut watermelon mixed with lemon zest. Grinding the flowers makes the citrus considerably sharper, introducing lemon oil, tropical fruit, mild earth, and occasionally a faint gassy edge. The sweetness never completely disappears, but it is balanced by enough acidity to keep the profile crisp.

Alien Labs identifies beta-caryophyllene, D-limonene, and beta-myrcene among the prominent terpenes in its Melonade. Limonene aligns naturally with the pronounced lemon character, while caryophyllene can contribute a drier spicy foundation and myrcene provides an earthy, fruity background. Actual terpene percentages remain crop-specific rather than fixed properties of the strain.

Flavor tends to open with tart citrus before ripe melon and sugary tropical notes expand across the palate. The exhale can become softer and creamier, with some expressions recalling sweet cereal or fruit candy. That balance of acidity and sweetness is more distinctive than simple fruitiness and remains one of the main reasons the cultivar developed such a strong following.
Growing Information

Melonade grows with more vigor and reach than a compact indica. Healthy plants develop strong lateral branching and enough internodal spacing for light to penetrate deeper into the canopy. Indoors, growers generally allow approximately eight to ten weeks for flowering, although historical descriptions of the original line include faster-finishing examples. Plant height is usually manageable with canopy training but can increase substantially once flowering begins.

Flower development can become dense despite the sativa-oriented effects and branching pattern. Resin accumulates heavily across mature buds, which contributed to the selected cut’s competition-quality appearance. As those flowers swell, air movement becomes increasingly important because tightly packed cannabis buds can retain moisture internally. Humidity control is particularly relevant during the final weeks.

Yield is generally considered medium to high rather than exceptional, and claims of precise gram-per-square-meter production should be treated cautiously because no single original breeder standard applies to every Melonade selection. Outdoors, warm conditions and plentiful sunlight can produce considerably larger plants, with harvest typically falling from late September into October depending on latitude, plant maturity, and local weather.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Melonade?

Melonade is Watermelon Zkittlez × Lemon Tree #11. Midwest Best created the cross using Watermelon Zkittlez from Dying Breed Seeds genetics and reversed Lemon Tree #11 pollen. Alien Labs helped select the keeper phenotype that became the best-known commercial version.
Is Melonade indica or sativa?

Melonade is generally regarded as a sativa-dominant hybrid, and Alien Labs markets its selected cut as a sativa. Its effects support that classification, with an energetic, euphoric cerebral phase appearing before stronger physical relaxation.
How strong is Melonade weed?

Modern flower commonly tests around 20–28% THC, although actual cannabinoid content depends on genetics, cultivation conditions, harvest maturity, and laboratory methodology. Consumers should use the test results from their specific product rather than assuming every batch has identical potency.
What does Melonade strain taste like?

The dominant flavors are lemon, watermelon, citrus, tropical fruit, and sweet melon. Lemon acidity usually arrives first, followed by softer fruit and candy-like sweetness. Alien Labs lists beta-caryophyllene, D-limonene, and beta-myrcene among the prominent terpenes in its commercial cut.
Did Melonade win a Cannabis Cup?

Yes. Melonade grown by Alien Labs won first place for Best Sativa Flower at the 2018 Central Valley Cannabis Cup. That early competition win became an important part of the cultivar’s reputation and helped introduce the strain to a much wider audience.
Final Thoughts on Melonade

Melonade arrived at a point when California cannabis was increasingly dominated by dense dessert genetics, yet its identity came from a brighter formula. Midwest Best’s pairing of Watermelon Zkittlez and Lemon Tree #11 produced a flower in which sharp citrus and soft melon sweetness remain equally important. Alien Labs’ selected expression then demonstrated the quality of that breeding work by capturing first place in the sativa flower category at the 2018 Central Valley Cannabis Cup.

Beyond the award, the cultivar earns attention through balance. Its aroma shifts between watermelon, lemon zest, tropical sweetness, and subtle earth; the effects move from cerebral enthusiasm toward comfortable physical ease; and the plant combines sativa-like branching with dense, resin-rich flowers. For cannabis enthusiasts drawn to fruity weed but looking for something sharper and more energetic than a conventional dessert hybrid, Melonade remains one of the defining citrus-melon cultivars of modern California breeding.
